statement: The Host queues each peer's messages up to a bound and drops the rest with a notice; the Host's own commands and timers have no peer's bound; a bound below one is refused.
source: spec/transport/link.scm (v1: a bounded inbound queue per peer, over the bound is loss); R-X1

layers.arrival: n/a: link.scm models no queue (a bound is loss, which its channel has) and spec/runtime/tick.scm has a lossless, unbounded queue with no sender's bound
layers.quint: n/a: spec/quint/runtime.qnt has a volatile inbox set (line 50), unbounded, not per sender, with no drop; a bound that drops is the Host's
layers.contract: n/a: a Host queue is off-chain
layers.rig: owed: test rig (a walk predicate for this rule; none is named yet)

killers.name: R-HOST-INBOX a sender over its bound is dropped with a notice; others and the Host's own queue on
R-HOST-INBOX a bound below one is refused when the limits are made, since such a Host could never move
